analysis: Both units are BASE-side excerpts of docs/threat-model.yaml. Unit :3 covers lines 473-889, spanning TB-007 (cache volume text), TB-009, TB-010, TB-011, TB-012 and T-007/T-008. Unit :4 covers lines 890-1395, spanning T-008 through T-041. Per file_changes, the base-side changed ranges in these units are TB-012 description and how_it_works (base 816-818, 821-829, 831). The patch excerpt shows the head TB-012 adding the operator lifecycle mailbox (darkbloom addon) as a same-user hold path. The changelog comment (head 46-49) also says TB-012 records accept-time peer checks, a socket override, self-reported busy fields and a fail-open hold record, T-059 adds a model-load fence, and new T-060 covers socket starvation and control-file read stalls. This is documentation only; no source code is in this batch. The head text beyond the truncated excerpt was not visible. Integration must verify the following in the head TB-012/T-059/T-060 text (head 820-862, 2349-2398) and the provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Addon/ sources: (1) Moving peer verification from per-request to accept-time is a material change. If a connection's identity is checked only at accept, a long-lived connection or fd passing/inheritance could let other same-UID code reuse a verified connection. Base line 821-822 said per-request LOCAL_PEERTOKEN checks. (2) The socket path override (env/config) could let same-UID code redirect the add-on, and must not apply in release builds. (3) The fail-open hold record means a corrupt or missing record releases the hold. This is availability-only, but it affects the A-018/T-059 assumptions. (4) The mailbox is unauthenticated against same-UID code, consistent with the base current_limitations at 833-836. (5) Busy fields are self-reported to the coordinator (A-018, TB-002); routing must not treat them as trust. No concrete regression is identifiable from the base-only text; the assumptions are listed for the head and source passes.
